args.note: Rigid gearbox attachment at x=0; entire end face clamped.

args.question: Should the 16 × 16 mm drive lugs be represented only by their load footprints, or should material behind them be preserved? I use z for height and y for depth: end-face footprints are y=32–48 mm, z=64–80 mm and z=0–16 mm. A pure 40 N·m torque uses opposite 625 N forces at their centres (64 mm apart). The choices below specify the upper lug; the lower lug receives the same treatment at z=0–16 mm.

options.label: Load footprints only; no prescribed solid lug volume.
Preserve 2 mm of solid material behind each footprint: x=158–160 mm.
Preserve 16 mm of solid material behind each footprint: x=144–160 mm.

result.question: Should the 16 × 16 mm drive lugs be represented only by their load footprints, or should material behind them be preserved? I use z for height and y for depth: end-face footprints are y=32–48 mm, z=64–80 mm and z=0–16 mm. A pure 40 N·m torque uses opposite 625 N forces at their centres (64 mm apart). The choices below specify the upper lug; the lower lug receives the same treatment at z=0–16 mm.

answer.comment: None of these is what the brief means. y is up. Both lugs sit inside the end face, flush with its top edge (y = 80) and bottom edge (y = 0), centred at z = 40, so their centres are 64 mm apart. Either sense is fine; take +x by the right-hand rule.

args.question: Using your clarified axes (y up, z depth) and +x torque, should the lugs be load footprints only, or preserved solid material with an axial depth? Each option below specifies the top lug; the bottom uses the same treatment at y=0–16 mm, z=32–48 mm. Loads will be +625 N in z on the top and −625 N in z on the bottom.

options.label: Face footprints only: 16 × 16 mm patches, no prescribed solid depth.
Preserve 2 mm depth behind both footprints, x=158–160 mm.
Preserve 16 mm depth behind both footprints, x=144–160 mm.

result.question: Using your clarified axes (y up, z depth) and +x torque, should the lugs be load footprints only, or preserved solid material with an axial depth? Each option below specifies the top lug; the bottom uses the same treatment at y=0–16 mm, z=32–48 mm. Loads will be +625 N in z on the top and −625 N in z on the bottom.

answer.label: Face footprints only: 16 × 16 mm patches, no prescribed solid depth.

args.description: 160×80×80 mm steel gearbox output bracket. y is up, z is depth. Entire x=0 face rigidly fixed. On x=160, 16×16 mm lug load footprints centred at (y,z)=(72,40) and (8,40), flush with y=80 and y=0 edges. Opposite ±625 N z forces give pure +x torque of 40000 N mm (40 N m), zero net force. Lugs are face footprints only, without passive solid depth, as clarified. Steel E=210000 N/mm², nu=0.3; design volume fraction 0.3; 2 mm elements.

args.note: Upper drive lug, y=64–80 mm, z=32–48 mm. +z force; one half of +x torque couple.
Lower drive lug, y=0–16 mm, z=32–48 mm. −z force; 64 mm centre separation gives +40000 N mm torque.
